metadata.title: Four agents, worse than one
metadata.topic: Anthropic's epistemic failure experiments — Figures 4 and 5
metadata.purpose: Show that Figure 4 contradicts its own caption, and that Figure 5's real result — deliberation is currently negative-value — was never written down.
metadata.gate: GATE P — not passed; no audio generated

beats.narration_text: Annyeong — this is Liam, in for Bear. Anthropic ran two experiments on multi-agent systems and wrote a blog post about what they found. The charts say something the text does not.

props.command: Hey Claude — if you put four AI agents in a room and each one holds a piece of the answer, do they find it?
props.runningText: reading the charts they did not label…

beats.narration_text: Hey Claude — if you put four AI agents in a room and each one holds a piece of the answer, do they find it?

props.command: Hey Claude — if you put four AI agents in a room and each one holds a piece of the answer, do they find it?

beats.narration_text: No. And the chart that shows how badly is the most important picture in Anthropic's whole post — which is strange, because the caption underneath it is about something else.

artifactLines: No.

beats.narration_text: Two experiments here. First, can an agent notice it is being lied to. Second, can a group of agents pool what they separately know. These are opposite skills, and that turns out to matter.

artifactLines: Two experiments here.
First, can an agent notice it is being lied to.
Second, can a group of agents pool what they separately know.
These are opposite skills, and that turns out to matter.

beats.narration_text: The lie test. A listener agent makes ten to fifteen decisions about a world it cannot see. Its only information comes from four scout agents whose reports partly overlap. One scout lies at a fixed rate.

artifactLines: The lie test.
A listener agent makes ten to fifteen decisions about a world it cannot see.
Its only information comes from four scout agents whose reports partly overlap.
One scout lies at a fixed rate.

beats.narration_text: Because the reports overlap, a lie is detectable in principle — it will eventually contradict an honest scout. The listener is never told anyone might be unreliable. It has to notice.

lines: Reports overlap: every lie will eventually contradict an honest scout.
The listener is never told anyone might be unreliable.
Detection requires the system to notice on its own.

beats.narration_text: Here is the result. Two reference lines: trust everyone, at the bottom, and learn who lies, at the top. Every model lands somewhere in between.
beats.credit: Anthropic Frontier Red Team, 'Patterns and problems in emerging multiagent systems', 13 Aug 2026 — published figure, reproduced for criticism

beats.narration_text: And here is the sentence printed with it: newer models recover more of the gap between the naive and oracle performances. This ordering holds across four different scenarios.
beats.credit: Anthropic Frontier Red Team, 13 Aug 2026 — verbatim text from the archived page, reproduced for criticism. Stylesheet was not archived; excerpt is typeset in the house serif, wording unaltered.
beats.new_visual_element: the claim, verbatim from the post, highlighted in situ

beats.narration_text: Let's compute that. Gap recovered equals the model, minus the naive line, divided by the distance to the oracle. At a fifty percent lie rate.

production_viz.label: animated Figure 4 — gap recovery computed per model
production_viz.note: silent 3840x2160 master, born native 4K; audit annotation already burned in

beats.new_visual_element: animated Figure 4 — gap recovery computed per model

beats.narration_text: Mythos 5 recovers ninety-one and a half percent. Opus 4.8, sixty-two and a half. Opus 4.6, fifty-nine point three. Sonnet 5 — which the post calls, quote, our most recent model — recovers thirty-seven point eight. And the older Sonnet 4.6, thirty-four point four.

production_viz.label: the ranked bars
production_viz.note: silent 3840x2160 master, born native 4K; audit annotation already burned in

beats.narration_text: Both Opus models are older, and both beat it. Only the previous Sonnet lands lower. Drop the lie rate to twenty-five percent, and Sonnet 5 is last of all five.

production_viz.label: the 0.25 crossover, isolated
production_viz.note: silent 3840x2160 master, born native 4K; audit annotation already burned in

beats.narration_text: So the ordering is not recency. It is capability tier — the Opus and Mythos lines sit above the Sonnet lines regardless of age. Which is a perfectly reasonable finding. It is just not the finding in the sentence.

artifactLines: So the ordering is not recency.
It is capability tier - the Opus and Mythos lines sit above the Sonnet lines regardless of age.

It is just not the finding in the sentence.

beats.narration_text: One more thing worth flagging. This figure's top line is labelled Mythos 5. Figure 1's top line is labelled Mythos Preview. The post never says which experiments used which model.

beats.narration_text: Second experiment, and this is the one. It's called a hidden profile, and psychologists have been running it on humans since nineteen eighty-five.

artifactLines: Second experiment, and this is the one.
It's called a hidden profile
and psychologists have been running it on humans since nineteen eighty-five.

beats.narration_text: Deal facts out to four participants so that everything they share points at the wrong answer, and the facts that decide it are held privately, one each. To win, somebody has to volunteer their private fact, and the rest have to believe them over the consensus.

lines: Shared facts all point to the wrong answer.
Each agent holds one decisive private fact.
Winning means volunteering it — and being believed.

beats.narration_text: Humans are famously bad at this. Discussion converges on what everybody already knew. The unshared fact never gets said, or gets said once and dropped.

artifactLines: Humans are famously bad at this.
Discussion converges on what everybody already knew.
The unshared fact never gets said, or gets said once and dropped.

beats.narration_text: Four hundred episodes per model. Hiring, investment, property. Here is the chart.
beats.credit: Anthropic Frontier Red Team, 'Patterns and problems in emerging multiagent systems', 13 Aug 2026 — published figure, reproduced for criticism
beats.new_visual_element: published Figure 5 — group accuracy by model

beats.narration_text: The caption talks about scaling: performance scales with model intelligence but does not saturate. Look at the three short bars.
beats.credit: Anthropic Frontier Red Team, 13 Aug 2026 — verbatim text from the archived page, reproduced for criticism. Stylesheet was not archived; excerpt is typeset in the house serif, wording unaltered.

beats.narration_text: Seventeen point five. Eighteen point five. Eighteen point two. Three models, spanning two generations, sitting inside each other's confidence intervals. That is a flat floor with two outliers, not a scaling curve.

production_viz.label: animated Figure 5 — with the deliberation cost drawn in
production_viz.note: silent 3840x2160 master, born native 4K; audit annotation already burned in

beats.new_visual_element: animated Figure 5 — with the deliberation cost drawn in

beats.narration_text: But that is the small finding. The big one is the dashed line above each bar.

production_viz.label: the solo-ceiling dashes appearing
production_viz.note: silent 3840x2160 master, born native 4K; audit annotation already burned in

beats.narration_text: That's the solo ceiling — one agent, holding all the facts, deciding alone. Ninety-six to one hundred percent. Every model solves this puzzle almost perfectly by itself.

production_viz.label: ceiling isolated
production_viz.note: silent 3840x2160 master, born native 4K; audit annotation already burned in

beats.narration_text: Now put four of them together and make them talk. Seventeen percent. Eighteen. Thirty-five. Even Mythos 5, the best of them, drops fifteen points.

production_viz.label: the red deliberation-cost boxes filling in
production_viz.note: silent 3840x2160 master, born native 4K; audit annotation already burned in

beats.new_visual_element: the red deliberation-cost boxes filling in

beats.narration_text: For every single model tested, group discussion made the group worse than one agent with the same information. Sixty to eighty percentage points worse, in four cases out of five.

artifactLines: For every single model tested
group discussion made the group worse than one agent with the same information.
Sixty to eighty percentage points worse, in four cases out of five.

beats.narration_text: That is the strongest result in the post. It is drawn on the chart. It is not in the caption.

artifactLines: That is the strongest result in the post.
It is drawn on the chart.
It is not in the caption.

beats.narration_text: Anthropic's framing of why is good, and I think correct. These two failures are opposites. Getting lied to punishes trusting too much. Hidden profiles punish trusting too little — the lone dissenter is right.

artifactLines: Anthropic's framing of why is good, and I think correct.
These two failures are opposites.
Getting lied to punishes trusting too much.
Hidden profiles punish trusting too little - the lone dissenter is right.

beats.narration_text: So there is no dial setting that fixes both. Humans didn't solve it with a dial either — we built reputation, courts, markets, peer review. Machinery that makes miscalibrated trust expensive in either direction.

artifactLines: So there is no dial setting that fixes both.
Humans didn't solve it with a dial either - we built reputation, courts, markets
peer review.
Machinery that makes miscalibrated trust expensive in either direction.

beats.narration_text: Agents have none of that. As the post puts it: they enter the market with no reputation to lose, no court to appeal to, and no colleague who remembers them.

artifactLines: Agents have none of that.
As the post puts it: they enter the market with no reputation to lose
no court to appeal to, and no colleague who remembers them.

beats.narration_text: Verdict. The lie-detection claim as written does not survive its own chart. The hidden-profile result does, and it is bigger than advertised: right now, agent deliberation is negative value. Adding agents to a decision makes the decision worse.

artifactLines: Verdict.
The lie-detection claim as written does not survive its own chart.
The hidden-profile result does, and it is bigger than advertised: right now
agent deliberation is negative value.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Try the hidden profile yourself. Split a decision's evidence across four separate chats so each one sees the shared facts plus one unique decisive fact, let them exchange summaries, and see whether the unique facts ever make it into the final answer. Then give one chat everything and compare.
